findings.summary: The page is titled and heroed as compute but contains one leftover compute use-case list followed by the entire networking chapter.
findings.evidence: "page_title":"Compute Services","hero":"ec2","subtitle":"From VMs to Serverless" — first block is "8. Use Cases", every block after it is "1. VPC", "2. Route 53", "3. Elastic Load Balancing", "4. CloudFront", "5. Direct Connect", "6. VPN", "7. Comparison", "8. Security in Networking".
findings.fix: Retitle to "AWS Networking Services" (hero "vpc", subtitle "Secure, Reliable, Scalable") and keep the compute "8. Use Cases" block on the compute page in Part 2, or label it explicitly "Compute, continued from Part 2".

findings.summary: Page 5 is titled and subtitled as the database chapter but contains no database content at all.
findings.evidence: "page_title":"AWS Database Services","subtitle":"RDS, Aurora, DynamoDB, ElastiCache" — the blocks are Route 53, CloudFront, VPC Peering, Transit Gateway, VPN, plus "1. The Hero Mark" and "4. The Motto"; the words RDS, Aurora, ElastiCache appear nowhere on the page (DynamoDB appears only as a build-example node on page 7).
findings.fix: Either retitle page 5 to match its actual content (e.g. "Networking: Peering, Transit Gateway, VPN") or replace the blocks with the promised RDS / Aurora / DynamoDB / ElastiCache sections.

findings.summary: The page is titled and heroed as database content but teaches only advanced networking and brand identity, with no database material anywhere on it.
findings.evidence: "page_title":"AWS Database Services" ... "hero":"rds","subtitle":"RDS, Aurora, DynamoDB, ElastiCache" — yet every block is networking ("1. Route 53 (DNS Service)", "3. CloudFront (CDN)", "4. VPC Peering", "5. Transit Gateway", "6. VPN Connection") or identity ("1. The Hero Mark", "4. The Motto").
findings.fix: Retitle the page "AWS Networking — Advanced" with hero "vpc" and subtitle "Route 53, CloudFront, Peering, TGW, VPN", and move the two identity blocks onto page 6 where the identity sections begin.

findings.summary: Pages 1 and 2 also carry titles that contradict their bodies, so three of eight pages mislabel their topic.
findings.evidence: Page 1: "page_title":"Compute Services","subtitle":"From VMs to Serverless" — after one "8. Use Cases" block every section is networking ("1. VPC", "2. Route 53", "3. Elastic Load Balancing", "4. CloudFront", "5. Direct Connect", "6. VPN"). Page 2: "page_title":"Networking Services" — after "10. Key Takeaways" every section is storage ("1. S3", "2. EBS", "3. EFS", "4. FSx", "5. S3 Glacier", "6. Storage Gateway").
findings.fix: Re-cut the page boundaries so each page_title/subtitle matches the sections it holds: move the trailing compute use-cases onto the compute page and the trailing networking recap onto the networking page, then title pages 1 and 2 "Networking Services" and "Storage Services" respectively.

findings.summary: Section numbering restarts and collides across consecutive pages, so a learner following the numbers cannot tell where they are in the part.
findings.evidence: Page 1 carries two blocks numbered 8 ("8. Use Cases" for compute and "8. Security in Networking"); page 3 runs "7. Comparison", "8. Key Features", "9. S3 Storage Classes" and page 4 then runs "6. Security Group vs Network ACL", "7. EBS Volume Types", "8. Key Takeaways".
findings.fix: Renumber sections continuously per chapter across the pages of this part, and when a chapter's numbering restarts, print the chapter name in the heading (e.g. "Storage 7. Comparison", "Security 6. Security Group vs NACL").

findings.summary: The caption's first sentence is an administrative label rather than a hook, so nothing stops the scroll.
findings.evidence: "Part 3 of AWS COMPLETE NOTES. Master AWS from Beginner to Advanced with this complete handwritten-notes handbook."
findings.fix: Lead with the value/curiosity line and demote the part label: "EC2, VPC, S3 classes, security groups and databases — the AWS pages that actually show up in interviews. (Part 3 of AWS COMPLETE NOTES.)"

findings.summary: Storage Gateway is described as having three gateway types; AWS offers four.
findings.evidence: "Types: File Gateway, Volume Gateway, Tape Gateway"
findings.fix: List all four current types: Amazon S3 File Gateway, Amazon FSx File Gateway, Volume Gateway, Tape Gateway.

findings.summary: The storage chapter's closing best-practices section is printed on page 2 while the sections it closes (comparison, key features, storage classes) only appear on page 3.
findings.evidence: Page 2 ends with "10. Best Practices" ("Choose the right storage service", "Enable versioning and lifecycle policies in S3"); page 3 then opens with "7. Comparison", "8. Key Features", "9. S3 Storage Classes".
findings.fix: Move the "10. Best Practices" block to the end of page 3, after "9. S3 Storage Classes", so sections run 1-10 in order.

findings.summary: Two networking diagrams (VPC architecture and DNS lookup) are dropped into the middle of the storage-comparison page, after the networking chapter already ended with its key takeaways.
findings.evidence: Page 3 contains "3. VPC Architecture (Example)" with the flowchart titled "VPC 10.0.0.0/16" and a second flowchart titled "DNS Lookup" (www.example.com → Route 53 → 192.0.2.10), placed between "9. S3 Storage Classes" and the storage tip callout; page 2 had already closed networking with "10. Key Takeaways".
findings.fix: Move both diagrams back beside their own sections — the VPC architecture flowchart under "1. VPC" on the networking page, the DNS lookup flowchart under "2. Route 53" — and leave page 3 purely storage.

findings.summary: The takeaway that an EBS volume serves exactly one EC2 instance is wrong for io1/io2 volumes, which support Multi-Attach.
findings.evidence: "EBS is block storage for ==one== EC2"
findings.fix: Reword to "EBS attaches to one EC2 instance at a time (io1/io2 Multi-Attach can attach one volume to up to 16 Nitro instances in the same AZ)".

findings.summary: The Security Group vs NACL table hangs its key distinction on the words stateful and stateless without ever saying what they mean in traffic terms.
findings.evidence: ["State","==Stateful==","==Stateless=="] is the only mention of either word on the page; the table has no return-traffic row and no surrounding text explaining the difference.
findings.fix: Add a "Return traffic" row — Security Group: "reply traffic allowed automatically"; Network ACL: "reply traffic needs its own explicit rule" — so the stateful/stateless labels are backed by observable behaviour.

findings.summary: Route 53 and CloudFront are introduced a second time as fresh numbered sections after both were already taught on page 1.
findings.evidence: Page 1: "2. Route 53" ("Highly available scalable DNS") and "4. CloudFront" ("CDN with low latency"). Page 5: "1. Route 53 (DNS Service)" ("Scalable ==DNS==: converts domain names to IP addresses") and "3. CloudFront (CDN)" ("==CDN== with low latency and high transfer speeds").
findings.fix: Keep one introduction of each service — teach Route 53 and CloudFront once on the networking page, and on the advanced page cover only the new material (routing policies, edge caching behaviour) under headings that say "recap" or "advanced".

findings.summary: The brand-identity sections run out of numeric order across the page break: section 4 is taught on page 5 before sections 2 and 3 on page 6, and section 1's diagram lands after section 4.
findings.evidence: Page 5 ends "1. The Hero Mark" then "4. The Motto"; page 6 opens with the flowchart "Hero Mark Placement" (section 1's diagram) then "2. Why a Cloud Mark", "3. Mark Rules".
findings.fix: Move "1. The Hero Mark" and its "Hero Mark Placement" diagram together to the top of page 6 and place "4. The Motto" after "3. Mark Rules", so the identity run reads 1, 2, 3, 4, 5.

findings.summary: The 10.0.2.0/24 subnet is labelled public in one VPC diagram and private in the other, so the two example architectures contradict each other.
findings.evidence: Page 1 diagram nodes: "Public Subnet 10.0.1.0/24", "Private Subnet 10.0.2.0/24"; page 3 flowchart nodes: "Public 10.0.1.0/24 (AZ A)", "Public 10.0.2.0/24 (AZ B)", "Private 10.0.3.0/24 (AZ A)".
findings.fix: Use one CIDR plan across both diagrams — e.g. public 10.0.1.0/24 and 10.0.2.0/24, private 10.0.3.0/24 and 10.0.4.0/24 — and update the page 1 diagram accordingly.

findings.summary: Section numbering is duplicated, out of order and skips a number across the part, so the numbered sequence cannot be followed.
findings.evidence: Page 1 contains "8. Use Cases" and later "8. Security in Networking"; page 2 ends with "10. Best Practices" while page 3 then opens with "7. Comparison", "8. Key Features", "9. S3 Storage Classes"; page 5 goes "1. Route 53" straight to "3. CloudFront" with no section 2.
findings.fix: Renumber each topic's sections in a single ascending sequence after the page re-cut, so no number repeats on a page and the storage sections 7–10 run in order.

findings.summary: #AWSIAM tags a service that no page in this part covers.

findings.summary: Direct Connect is presented as inherently secure and faster, but a DX link is private and unencrypted by default and offers consistent, not necessarily higher, bandwidth.
findings.evidence: "Dedicated network connection to AWS" / "More reliable, secure and faster"
findings.fix: Replace with "Private, consistent-bandwidth connection that bypasses the public internet; traffic is NOT encrypted by default — add MACsec or a VPN over Direct Connect for encryption."
